units.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Agents
topics: Seeing the ideas: people, machines, agents and environments

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: people, machines, agents and environments

summary: AI is the study of agents that act rationally. Four definitions (thinking or acting, humanly or rationally) co-exist; the rational-agent view is the most used.
Weak AI solves specific tasks and is the only AI that exists; strong AI is a general machine mind and remains a hypothesis.
AI draws on philosophy, mathematics, economics, neuroscience, psychology and computing; its history alternates enthusiasm and AI winters.
An agent maps percepts to actions; PEAS specifies its task; agents range from simple reflex to learning agents; the environment type determines how hard the task is.

units.title: Problem Solving Methods
topics: Seeing the ideas: puzzles, people, games and traced searches

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: puzzles, people, games and traced searches

summary: A search problem is defined by states, actions, a goal test and path costs; the algorithm determines which frontier node is expanded next.
BFS, UCS and IDDFS are complete; BFS and IDDFS are optimal for equal step costs and UCS for any positive costs; DFS saves memory but is neither.
A* with an admissible (tree) or consistent (graph) heuristic is optimal and more efficient than blind search; a dominant heuristic expands fewer nodes.
Local search keeps one state and suits optimisation; simulated annealing escapes local maxima by occasionally accepting worse moves.
CSPs are solved by backtracking with MRV and forward checking. Games are searched by minimax; alpha–beta gives the same answer with far fewer nodes.

units.title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
topics: Seeing the ideas: logicians, rules, networks and probabilities

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: logicians, rules, networks and probabilities

summary: Knowledge can be held as rules, semantic networks, frames or logic; a good scheme is adequate, inferentially efficient and easy to extend.
Propositional logic gives sound, complete reasoning by truth table or resolution; Horn clauses allow efficient forward and backward chaining.
First-order logic adds objects, relations and quantifiers; unification and resolution (with Skolemisation) prove theorems mechanically; Prolog implements the idea.
Under uncertainty, probability and Bayes' rule update beliefs; Bayesian networks factor the joint distribution into small CPTs and answer queries by enumeration or sampling.

units.title: Learning
topics: Forms of learning in the syllabus
Seeing the ideas: pioneers, flowers, evolution and the algorithms

sections.title: Forms of learning in the syllabus
Seeing the ideas: pioneers, flowers, evolution and the algorithms

summary: Machine learning improves a task from data: supervised (labelled), unsupervised (structure), reinforcement (rewards); evaluate on unseen data to detect overfitting.
Rote learning memorises, analogy reuses similar cases, induction generalises, explanation-based learning generalises from one explained example.
Decision trees split on the attribute with the highest information gain; naive Bayes multiplies class-conditional probabilities; k-NN votes among nearest neighbours.
Genetic algorithms evolve a population with selection, crossover and mutation.

units.title: Neural Networks and Natural Language Processing
topics: Feedback networks: Hopfield network and Boltzmann machine
Seeing the ideas: neurons, perceptrons, networks and language

sections.title: Feedback networks: Hopfield network and Boltzmann machine
Seeing the ideas: neurons, perceptrons, networks and language

summary: An artificial neuron sums weighted inputs and applies an activation; a perceptron learns linearly separable functions (AND, OR) but not XOR.
Hidden layers and back-propagation (the chain rule applied layer by layer) let networks learn non-linear functions; training is gradient descent on a loss.
Hopfield networks store patterns as energy minima and recall them from noisy input while the load stays below about 0.14 N patterns; Boltzmann machines add stochastic units.
NLP converts text to meaning by lexical, syntactic, semantic, discourse and pragmatic analysis; n-gram, edit-distance and TF-IDF methods are the classical statistical tools.

units.title: Expert Systems and Machine Vision
topics: Seeing the ideas: expert systems and machine vision

sections.title: Seeing the ideas: expert systems and machine vision

summary: An expert system captures a specialist's rules in a knowledge base used by a general inference engine, explains its reasoning and handles uncertainty with certainty factors; it is brittle outside its domain and costly to maintain.
Development goes from identification through formalisation to testing and maintenance, with the knowledge engineer bridging expert and program.
Machine vision turns pixels into decisions by acquisition, preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction and recognition; edge detection is a convolution with kernels such as Sobel's.
Both technologies serve real applications in industry, health and agriculture, with privacy, bias and accountability concerns.
